question: How do receptacle entry latching, attachment/item transfers, one-time brain feedback and six-record restart interact?

semantics.dispatch: Counted descriptor traversal first skips NULL state and outside-view bit0 of interaction_flags. Within world_object_flags, checkpoint role bit4 wins over receptacle bit2, then proximity-animation bit0. Inactive player bit1 skips receptacle handling. Transfer success returns from the entire service; rejected/latched/far paths continue the counted scan.
semantics.distance: Descriptor WORD XY plus state WORD offsets, then16 on each axis; player WORD XY also plus16. Subtractions, signed-negative magnitude and sum wrap modulo65536. Unsigned wrapped sum below28 enters range. Full signed-minimum magnitude stays8000. This is not unbounded Manhattan distance.
semantics.entry_latch: Near handling sets interaction flags bit0 before phase/item checks. An already-set bit skips all following work; even a busy hand or incorrect return consumes the attempt. The first attempt clears movement_commit_inhibited. Far handling clears only bit0, retaining other flag bits; NULL interaction data is guarded only on that far path. No fire-button check.
semantics.pickup: Historic deposit_item_in_receptacle copies state.attachment_state_ptr into data.stored_attachment_state_ptr, clears the state pointer and gives the unfiltered required ID to player.selected_item_id. Held IDs0/1 qualify, IDs2..255 skip. NULL attachment is not rejected. Selected-name refresh is called, then non-brain or already-latched brain returns from the entire service. Existing public names remain unchanged.
semantics.return: A nonzero saved attachment chooses exact BYTE required/held comparison, including IDs0/1. Match restores the saved attachment into the state, clears the saved pointer and selected ID, then tail-returns through selected-name refresh. Mismatch attempts incorrect-item and blank scrolling messages, retaining phase/item values and continuing to a second descriptor in the complete witness.
semantics.brain: Required item ID104 takes the existing one-time event-bit0 path. First pickup assigns the full HP WORD95 even from96,255 or65535; it does not add or clamp upward. Original health drawing and feedback sequence011C complete; A4 becomes health overlay and A5 player. With event bit0 already set, pickup still transfers item while skipping HP/display/audio effect. Native analysis has one observed direct caller of this feedback entry; indirect-caller closure is not asserted.
semantics.restart: The original six-LONG table has a24-byte owner and no sentinel. Each of six visits clears the whole interaction flags BYTE. Nonzero saved pointer restores attachment and is cleared; NULL preserves current attachment. Shared interaction data is consumed by the first state, so later aliases preserve theirs. Required item IDs survive. All64 saved-pointer presence masks are covered on the six original records.

coverage.execution_notes: Twenty-one initially passing cases were retained. The comparison fixture was corrected to supply its required A3 input. The six brain cases use a fresh independent call frame after real audio initialization. The wrong-return witness was strengthened and rerun to visit a second NULL-state descriptor. The final33 distinct cases are covered by the successful focused runs; unchanged cases were not repeated.
coverage.ui_scope: Selected-name refresh is invoked in inventory-panel mode4 and returns immediately. Six brain witnesses execute real health drawing and original audio initialization/feedback. Flat16MB RAM supplies MMIO shadow values and valid original UI/font/audio data. Bounded write summaries may overflow; guest memory and normal return are checked.
